blocks.md:
1. **A demanding test.** AB 1228 raised the floor for large fast-food chains from the \$16 state minimum to \$20 on April 1, 2024 (+25%, about 77% of the state median wage), with customers able to switch to uncovered restaurants.
2. **Earnings up about 7%.** In limited-service restaurants relative to states at the \$7.25 federal minimum.
3. **Employment roughly unchanged.** Synthetic DiD gives −0.26 (0.54) log points (QCEW) and +0.74 (QWI); conventional DiD −1.39. Separations fell sharply, consistent with lower quits.
What happened to fast-food earnings and employment in California after AB 1228?

Limited-service restaurants (NAICS 722513), covered and uncovered, in two UI-based sources: [Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW)](note:quarterly-census-of-employment-and-wages-qcew) through 2025Q3 and the Quarterly Workforce Indicators (QWI, with worker flows) through 2024Q4. Controls: 20 states at the federal minimum. Outcome: log jobs per capita; weights fit on 2015Q1–2023Q4 excluding 2020–21, with 2024Q1 dropped as a transition quarter.

[Synthetic difference-in-differences](note:synthetic-control): California's employment rate had been converging toward control states, so simple parallel trends may fail. SDID chooses state weights so controls track California's pre-policy path up to a constant gap, and time weights so the controls' weighted past predicts their post-policy average.

blocks.md: Own-wage elasticity −0.04 (SDID) versus −0.19 (conventional DiD). Across 16 QWI specifications employment estimates run from about −0.6% to +1.7%. Earnings gains and separation declines are larger at large employers.

- One treated state; inference and estimates depend on donor pool and design choices (see Clemens, Edwards, Meer and Nguyen 2026).
- Employers could adjust between enactment (September 2023) and implementation.
- Short post-period.
